summary.title: The Website Specification
summary.one_liner: A platform-agnostic reference of technical features a good website should have, organised into ten areas with a yes/no audit checklist.
takeaways: The spec covers ten areas: Foundations, SEO, Accessibility, Security, Well-Known URIs, Agent Readiness, Performance, Privacy, Resilience, and Internationalisation.
Each topic explains what it is, why it matters, and how to implement it, grounded in primary web standards.
The checklist rates items as Required, Recommended, Optional, or Avoid, and each item is a yes/no question.
You can audit a site against the checklist, fix gaps, and re-check.
An open, read-only MCP server lets an AI agent query the specification; no authentication is needed for the reference tools.
summary.summary: The Website Specification is a platform-agnostic guide to the technical features a good website should have, built in the open under an MIT licence. It is organised into ten areas (for example Foundations, SEO, Accessibility, Security, Performance, and Privacy) containing around 20 to 30 topics each, with the topic counts shown on the page. Every topic explains what the feature is, why it matters, and how to implement it. A separate checklist lets you audit a site with yes/no items grouped by priority, and the page also links to an MCP server for querying the spec.
